title: Positivity in Symmetric Webs and Block Permanents

numbered_results.description: Matrix inequality for every stated case, including the threshold and its logarithmic consequence.
Two quadratic packets. Direct expansion identifies the permanent difference with four times the one-cap energy.
Both digon identities for the actual symmetric split and merge.
Homogeneous and isometric Schur identities in the finite-dimensional representation, for arbitrary sizes. The proof counts permutation double cosets.
Clasp recursion on ordinary words from the one-strand Schur relation.
The trace cup has closed value equal to the dimension. The reverse composite on a product is its evaluation times the trace cup.
Partial transpose preserves the quadratic-form evaluation on a product when the marked input is conjugated.
The bent Schur operator is the binomially weighted sum of actual cap-adjoint products.
Exact orthogonal decomposition of the Gram form at a cut.
Fine and packet closures equal the respective permanents. The polarized identity allows distinct packets on the two sides.
Exact two-block gap on symmetric packets at every positive thickness, including the empty sum of proper cuts.
Rectangular Schur opening on all ordinary and marked word coordinates, including the zero and terminal terms.
Transfer under simultaneous upper/lower relabeling, including the tensor-coordinate representation.
Corrected bend with the two full caps and their mixed terms, for arbitrary thickness and positive ordinary packet count.
Exact three-packet raw opening of the original marked operator, including the negative terminal square.
Supported trace bubble and last-cap decomposition, with the perpendicular component retained.

Supported decomposition and positivity on an arbitrary marked subspace of the stated dimension. This establishes the stronger operator statement independently of the matching proof of the matrix inequality.
The iterated transfer has the printed coefficient for each routing. Clasp insertion identifies the coefficient recurrence with the actual operator iteration.
Split-end coefficient in the signed marked transfer, on the representation of actual strand permutations.

Each clasped routed Gram is scalar on its occupation sector. The generalized inverse of the sector blocks gives the orthogonal projector onto the sum of the reflected cap images, also for an arbitrary marked subspace.
Gram entries on each sector, nonsingular Gram estimate, and projection onto the span using the generalized inverse in the singular case.
Four-packet marked transfer, support under the clasp, and its simultaneous average. See the proof correction below.
All three families of open cuts, with the signed terminal terms, on the actual four-packet word boundary.
Positive compression on the whole space supported by an arbitrary marked subspace of dimension at most two, and the four-quadratic PSD matrix consequence.
Balanced opening with the two crossing pairings, proper caps and terminal terms.
Last-cap coefficients and the individual trace-cup remainders on the two independently marked subspaces.
Positivity of each supported balanced compression for thickness at least four, followed by the four-block matrix inequality.
Signed gluing identity at every positive real parameter.
Four cubic packets in every Gram dimension. Includes the signed square certificate and its PSD matrix consequence.
Pair lower bound and the actual residual halfweb Gram factor on arbitrary symmetric second inputs, including its polarized form.
Fine matching bound on matrix packets. The averaged identity retains the positive cut remainder.
Packet peel identity, including its exact exit-square remainder and the average over the marked packet.
Matching-moment upper bound for the Gram permanent, with the stated deletion recurrence for its coefficients.
The general matrix threshold follows both from the earlier integer-weight comparison and from the manuscript’s Jacobi spectrum and Maclaurin estimate.
Parameterized four-face trade, including the reflected-square difference for all positive parameters.
The tridiagonal PSD condition gives the claimed bound on every PSD block matrix. Pivot elimination and parameter trades give the signed square certificate on unit packets.
Unordered two-step path bound, with incident exterior squares and opposite-edge reflected squares.
Five matrix packets of thickness at least three in every Gram dimension. The five-packet expansion has its own exact certificate.
Positive free-cable form and the full test with explicit proper-cut remainders. The uniform coefficient is 41/20.
Reflected Gram trace for arbitrary admissible parameters and the plain and spectator-weighted averages.
Both long-cycle inequalities with the squared differences retained.
Five actual plane quadratics give a negative fifth marked closure. The witness is evaluated using the whole clasps.
Exact three- and four-subset exit sums with the printed coefficients and the individual weighted remainders.
The physical four-face slack summed once per actual face and disjoint matching, including its recurrence, boundary values and nonnegative remainder.
Both signs of the unnormalized odd-cycle cut, with actual matching masses and oriented cycles, including the smallest permitted label set.
Both signs on each cycle type. Local reflected energies multiply over disjoint assignments, with the parity factor, and the class-size sum yields the matrix criterion.
Occupation coefficient for a routed cap and the complex Gram seam with its occupation norm factors.
Forced-edge factorization, polynomial extraction, and the marked readout on the quadratic packets used in this appendix.
Direct 24 and 8 permanent values, with the gap 16 counted by permutations which split both packets.
Direct complex matching term, cap matrix, squared norm 5/2 and gap 10.
Direct 2+1 fork on the clasped word with two identical letters, with weights 1/3 and 2/3.
Direct interchange on alternating tensors and positive cap–cup after bending.
Direct two- and three-strand bent expansions.
Direct nontrivial four-strand cut values and total gap 14.
Direct three-quadratic opening, including the surviving upright term.
Direct evaluation of the four terms on the indicated unaveraged boundary, and their identity after relabeling.
Direct surviving terms, zero perpendicular part, normalized gap 84 and raw permanents 720 and 48.
Direct one-strand bubble, crossed gluing and the behavior of reflected images on the marked line and its orthogonal complement.
Direct three-placement expansion, the single surviving term and the final clasp factor 1/3.
Direct Gram matrix and the single- and joint-projection energies 1/2 and 2/3.
Direct cubic shortfall with single-edge budget 9 and coherent energy 16.
Direct middle matrix, trace, squared norm and equality on the orthonormal pair.
Direct four-label evaluations of the one- and two-matching moments.
Four- and five-packet threshold comparison and the four-label coefficient polynomial.
Direct exact tridiagonal pivots, PSD certificate and six-block consequence.
Direct cap energies of the orthogonal cubic and its disjoint pair cuts.
Direct unit Gram constructions with opposite signed triangle terms.
Two marked ends and the five coefficients of the pictured routing.
Direct polynomial for a triangle, a transposition and an allocated fixed point, and class size 120.
Exact ten-label coefficient table and resulting thickness range.
Direct evaluation of the reflected vector, its squared norm 1/2 and the glued seam value 1/2.
Direct rational fine and coarse closures, all five marks, their mean and agreement with the forced-edge calculation.

proof_notes.name: Remark after Example 3A.4
proof_notes.description: The open bend has a nonzero witness of eigenvalue −2 at thickness at least two. The fine cuts vanish on that witness.

proof_notes.name: Correction in the proof of Lemma 5B.1
proof_notes.description: After averaging over four packet labels, the identity is [B]₄ = [X₃]₄. The printed conclusion for [Q]₄ follows.
